# Crawl files: robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt

These files are generated artifacts. Generate them from the same source of truth as
the HTML so they never drift, and validate them in CI.

## robots.txt

Minimum for a public site:

```txt
# Generated by the build. Change the generator, not this file.

User-agent: *
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml
```

Rules:
- Place it at the host root (`https://example.com/robots.txt`); paths in `Disallow` are
  relative to the host.
- Point at every sitemap (or a sitemap index) with absolute URLs.
- Keep public content crawlable. Do not add accidental `Disallow: /` for staging
  leftover reasons.

### AI crawler policy (decide separately)

AI **search/answer** crawlers let the site be cited in answers. AI **model-training**
crawlers harvest content for training. They are different decisions; encode them
explicitly instead of hiding behind the wildcard group.

```txt
# AI search and answer engines: allowed so the site can be cited.
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /
User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /
User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /
User-agent: Claude-SearchBot
Allow: /
User-agent: Gemini-DeepResearch
Allow: /

# Model-training crawlers: opted out (change only with a deliberate decision).
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /
User-agent: CCBot
Disallow: /
User-agent: Google-Extended
Disallow: /
User-agent: Applebot-Extended
Disallow: /
User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /
User-agent: anthropic-ai
Disallow: /
User-agent: Bytespider
Disallow: /
```

Notes:
- `Google-Extended` does not affect Google Search; it controls Gemini training/grounding
  usage. `Googlebot` remains governed by the wildcard/specific group.
- Groups override the wildcard for matching bots. Keep the policy documented in the
  report; changing it is a business decision, not a technical fix.
- robots.txt cannot remove a page from search results. Use `noindex` or remove the URL.
- AI crawler user-agent names change over time; verify the current list before shipping
  and keep the file easy to edit.

## sitemap.xml

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9"
        xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/</loc>
    <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/"/>
    <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="fr" href="https://example.com/fr/"/>
    <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/"/>
  </url>
</urlset>
```

Rules:
- Only canonical, 200, indexable URLs. One `<loc>` per URL; do not list redirects or
  duplicates.
- Multilingual: each URL carries the full alternate set (including self and
  `x-default`), exactly matching the `<head>` hreflang block.
- `<lastmod>` must reflect real content changes.
- Validate: XML parse + every `<loc>` responds 200 + alternates point to existing pages.
- If you generate the sitemap, run the same generator in CI and diff the URL count.

## llms.txt

`llms.txt` is a proposed convention for AI tools: a short, maintained Markdown summary
with links to accurate public pages. It complements — never replaces — HTML, sitemap,
structured data, or robots.txt.

```md
# Example Co

> Example Co helps small businesses organize sales, stock, invoices, payments and
> digital workflows. It works remotely with customers in Haiti, the diaspora and other
> supported markets.

Example Co provides setup, support, training and selected AI-assisted workflows.
Availability, payment options and integrations depend on the customer's location and
requirements. AI outputs may require human review.

## Services
- [Sales, stock and invoicing](https://example.com/services/sales-stock-invoicing/): Track sales, inventory and customer invoices.
- [Digital payments](https://example.com/services/digital-payments/): Explore supported payment connections.

## Languages
- [English](https://example.com/en/)
- [Français](https://example.com/fr/)

## Contact
- [Website](https://example.com/)
- [Sitemap](https://example.com/sitemap.xml)
```

Rules:
- Keep it short and accurate; link only public, canonical pages.
- Localize only if you maintain each version; otherwise ship one accurate language and
  say so.
- Do not stuff keywords or duplicate the whole site. It is a summary, not a second site.
- Update it with the same build/PR that changes the catalog; stale summaries are worse
  than none.

## Validation commands

```bash
curl -sSI https://example.com/robots.txt | head -5
curl -sS https://example.com/robots.txt
curl -sS https://example.com/sitemap.xml | grep -c '<loc>'
node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('sitemap.xml','utf8'); new (require('vm').Script)(s.slice(0,0)||'')"  # XML: use a real parser in CI
```

Prefer the bundled auditor (`node scripts/seo-audit.mjs crawl-files <url|dir>`), which
checks XML structure, sitemap/robots agreement, alt sets, and llms.txt shape.
